lessons.title: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan's Upper West Side. New Yorkers are captivated
lessons.title_zh: 一隻罕見的倉鴞家族搬進了曼哈頓上西城，紐約人為之著迷

paragraphs.en: A family of barn owls has recently made a home inside a water tower on a building in Manhattan's Upper West Side. According to a migration ecologist, this marks the first recorded instance of these birds nesting in Manhattan in modern history.
paragraphs.zh: 一隻倉鴞家族最近在曼哈頓上西城一棟建築物的水塔內築巢安家。根據一位遷徙生態學家的說法，這是現代史上首次記錄到這些鳥類在曼哈頓築巢。

paragraphs.en: The discovery began when a local resident and her husband noticed multiple owls near Central Park and notified a news outlet. Soon after, photographers and curious onlookers began gathering on the street every night to catch a glimpse of the rare birds.
paragraphs.zh: 這個發現始於一位當地居民和她的丈夫注意到中央公園附近有多隻貓頭鷹，並通報了一家新聞媒體。不久之後，攝影師和好奇的圍觀民眾開始每晚聚集在街上，希望能一睹這些罕見鳥類的風采。

paragraphs.en: Experts note that barn owl sightings are extremely rare in New York City parks because the city sits at the northern fringe of their range. Furthermore, local residents initially heard bizarre screeching noises for weeks before realizing that the sounds came from owls.
paragraphs.zh: 專家指出，在紐約市公園裡發現倉鴞的機率極低，因為該市位於其活動範圍的北端邊緣。此外，當地居民在意識到這些聲音是貓頭鷹發出之前，最初連續幾週聽到奇怪的尖叫聲。

paragraphs.en: Despite the strange noises, people on the Upper West Side are thrilled by the unexpected visitors. As one resident expressed, having a family breeding in Manhattan is truly special news for both bird watchers and the general public.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管有奇怪的噪音，上西城的人們仍為這些意料之外的訪客感到興奮。正如一位居民所表達的，有一個家族在曼哈頓繁殖，對於賞鳥人士和大眾來說確實是特別的新聞。

grammar.explain: 用關代which引導形容詞子句，修飾前面的先行詞a building。
grammar.example: A family of barn owls has recently made a home inside a water tower on a building in Manhattan's Upper West Side.
grammar.focus: on a building in Manhattan's Upper West Side

grammar.explain: 使用現在分詞notifying引導分詞構句，補充說明前面的主詞動作。
grammar.example: The discovery began when a local resident and her husband noticed multiple owls near Central Park and notified a news outlet.

lessons.title: To train robots, AI companies are paying people in India to film themselves doing chores
lessons.title_zh: 為了訓練機器人，人工智慧公司付錢請印度人拍攝自己做家事的影片

paragraphs.en: In various parts of India, people receive payment to record themselves performing everyday household tasks. Technology developers are currently working to train artificial intelligence robots so that these machines can manage domestic chores effectively.
paragraphs.zh: 在印度的不同地區，人們獲得報酬來記錄自己執行日常家務工作。科技開發人員目前正在努力訓練人工智慧機器人，以便這些機器能夠有效地管理家務。

paragraphs.en: A reporter from National Public Radio visited a small town in southern India named Karur earlier this month. She discovered a growing commercial sector where people make videos of themselves cleaning or cooking. For example, twenty-four-year-old Sneha Jegadish attaches a smartphone to a headset to capture her hand movements while she prepares meals.
paragraphs.zh: 國家公共廣播電台的一名記者本月初造訪了印度南部一個名為卡魯爾的小鎮。她發現了一個不斷成長的商業領域，人們在其中拍攝自己打掃或煮飯的影片。例如，二十四歲的斯妮哈·傑加迪許將智慧型手機夾在耳機上，以便在她準備餐點時捕捉她的手部動作。

paragraphs.en: Industry experts note that thousands of individuals across the country take on this job. Participants spend a few hours daily folding clothes or washing dishes, which can bring in about $120 each month. Because web data cannot teach machines physical actions, these massive video collections are necessary to supply the required information.
paragraphs.zh: 產業專家指出，全國有數千名個人從事這項工作。參與者每天花費數小時摺衣服或洗碗，這大約能帶來每個月120美元的收入。由於網路資料無法教導機器肢體動作，這些大量的影片合集對於提供所需的資訊是必要的。

paragraphs.en: Prathosh A.P., a professor at the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru who specializes in machine-learning systems, explains this concept. He mentions that current systems act like brains without bodies, so they need physical training to develop necessary motor skills. This demand has provided business opportunities for local firms such as Objectways.
paragraphs.zh: 班加羅爾印度科學研究所專精於機器學習系統的教授普拉托什·A·P解釋了這個概念。他提到現今的系統就像沒有身體的大腦，因此牠們需要體能訓練來發展必要的運動技能。這項需求為當地的企業（例如Objectways）提供了商機。

paragraphs.en: Inside the company buildings, employees have built mock living rooms and kitchens to record high-quality training footage. Rani N., one of the workers, records herself wiping tables and cutting vegetables in a model kitchen. Company staff believe that humanoid helpers could eventually retail in the region, bringing much-needed rest to family caregivers.
paragraphs.zh: 在公司建築內部，員工建造了模擬客廳與廚房來錄製高品質的訓練片段。其中一位員工拉妮·N在樣品廚房中錄製自己擦拭桌子和切蔬菜的過程。公司員工相信，人形幫手最終可能在該地區零售，為家庭照顧者帶來急需的休息。

grammar.explain: 用來修飾先行詞，補充說明其詳細特徵。
grammar.example: Technology developers are currently working to train artificial intelligence robots so that these machines can manage domestic chores effectively.

grammar.explain: 強調動作的承受者，結構為 be 動詞加上過去分詞。
grammar.example: A reporter from National Public Radio visited a small town in southern India named Karur earlier this month.

grammar.point: 不定詞表目的 (Infinitive of purpose)
grammar.explain: 置於句中用以說明某個動作的目的或原因。
grammar.example: Inside the company buildings, employees have built mock living rooms and kitchens to record high-quality training footage.

lessons.title: How an accelerating Earth led experts to adopt the leap hour
lessons.title_zh: 地球加速自轉如何促使專家採用「閏時」

paragraphs.en: For decades, scientists have worried about the way computers handle time. At a meeting in France, representatives from 69 nations voted to remove the leap second and prepare for a leap hour instead. The International Bureau of Weights and Measures decided this change to protect modern technical networks. When a minute has 61 or 59 seconds, computer software often suffers serious errors.
paragraphs.zh: 幾十年來，科學家一直擔心電腦處理時間的方式。在法國舉行的一場會議上，來自六十九個國家的代表投票決定取消「閏秒」，改為準備實施「閏時」。國際度量衡局做出這項改變是為了保護現代技術網路。當一分鐘有六十一秒或五十九秒時，電腦軟體往往會出現嚴重錯誤。

paragraphs.en: Since 1967, one second has been defined by the steady vibrations of caesium atoms. These atomic clocks provide accurate time for electricity grids, satellites, and communications. However, the rotation of the Earth is not as reliable. Because natural forces such as ocean shifts affect the planet, our world generally spins more slowly than atomic time. To solve this, officials added 27 leap seconds between 1972 and recent years.
paragraphs.zh: 自1967年以來，一秒鐘是根據銫原子穩定的振動來定義的。這些原子鐘為電網、衛星和通訊提供了精確的時間。然而，地球的自轉並沒有那麼可靠。由於海洋移動等自然力量影響著這顆星球，我們的世界自轉速度通常比原子時間慢。為了解決這個問題，官方在1972年至近年之間增加了二十七個閏秒。

paragraphs.en: Recently, the Earth has actually started to spin faster. Scientists saw a 30 percent chance that a negative leap second might be needed soon. This would mean subtracting a second from the official time. In 2012, an extra second caused computer servers to freeze, bringing down websites like Reddit and LinkedIn, and delaying Qantas flights. Experts warned that subtracting a second would carry even greater risks because software has never been tested for it.
paragraphs.zh: 最近，地球實際上開始轉得更快了。科學家發現有百分之三十的機率很快就需要一個負閏秒。這意味著要從官方時間中減去一秒。在2012年，多出的一秒導致電腦伺服器當機，使Reddit和LinkedIn等網站癱瘓，並延誤了澳洲航空的航班。專家警告，減去一秒會帶來更大的風險，因為軟體從未針對這種情況進行過測試。

paragraphs.en: Under the new plan, Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) will be allowed to drift by up to an full hour before any adjustment occurs. A leap hour is not expected to happen for thousands of years. Dr Setnam Shemar, an expert from the UK's National Physical Laboratory (NPL), noted that adding an hour would resemble daylight saving time, which people already know. While some officials pointed out that this vote merely delays the issue for future generations, it successfully shields modern technology from immediate digital chaos.
paragraphs.zh: 在新計畫下，世界協調時間（UTC）將被允許在進行任何調整之前，出現最多達整整一小時的誤差。預計幾千年內都不會發生閏時。來自英國國家物理實驗室（NPL）的專家塞特南·謝馬爾博士指出，增加一小時就像人們已經熟悉的日光節約時間。儘管一些官員指出這次投票只不過是將問題延後給後代處理，但它成功保護了現代科技免於立即陷入數位混亂。

grammar.point: 不定詞表目的 (Infinitive of Purpose)
grammar.explain: 句中的「to protect」為不定詞片語，用來表示國際度量衡局做出這項決定的目的或原因。
grammar.example: The International Bureau of Weights and Measures decided this change to protect modern technical networks.

grammar.point: 現在完成被動態 (Present Perfect Passive)
grammar.explain: 由「has been」搭配過去分詞「defined」構成，表示從過去持續到現在已被界定的動作狀態。
grammar.example: Since 1967, one second has been defined by the steady vibrations of caesium atoms.

grammar.point: 非限定關係子句 (Non-restrictive Relative Clause)
grammar.explain: 逗號後的「which people already know」為非限定關係子句，以關係代名詞「which」補充說明前面的「daylight saving time」。
grammar.example: Dr Setnam Shemar, an expert from the UK's National Physical Laboratory (NPL), noted that adding an hour would resemble daylight saving time, which people already know.

lessons.title: Tesla unveils what it says is a flying car
lessons.title_zh: 特斯拉揭曉其宣稱的飛天車

paragraphs.en: Tesla CEO Elon Musk recently unveiled a new sports car model during an event at a test facility in Texas. The vehicle is designed to go from 0 to 60 mph in less than a second and features unique capabilities that allow it to jump and hover using specialized air jets.
paragraphs.zh: 特斯拉（Tesla）執行長馬斯克（Elon Musk）最近在德州的一處測試設施舉辦的活動中，揭曉了一款新的跑車車型。該車輛的設計能在不到一秒的時間內從靜止加速到每小時 60 英里，並具備獨特的功能，允許它透過專門的空氣噴射器進行跳躍和懸停。

paragraphs.en: During the product demonstration, the sports car performed several stunts without an actual driver inside to ensure safety. The vehicle used the built-in air jets to leap over parked company vehicles and demonstrated rapid acceleration on the test track.
paragraphs.zh: 在產品示範期間，這輛跑車在內部沒有真實駕駛的情況下執行了多項特技，以確保安全。該車輛利用內建的空氣噴射器飛躍停放的公司車輛，並在測試跑道上展示了快速加速。

paragraphs.en: Despite the successful demonstration, experts question whether a street-legal vehicle can truly fly and meet owners' expectations. Officials noted that building a hybrid between an aircraft and a ground vehicle often results in a poor-performing vehicle and a poor-performing plane.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管示範取得成功，專家們仍質疑道路合法車輛是否能真正飛行並符合車主的期望。官方指出，建造介於飛機與地面車輛之間的混合體，通常會導致性能不佳的車輛與性能不佳的飛機。

paragraphs.en: Other companies working on electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, known as eVTOLs, point out that the transition from vertical lifting to forward movement is extremely difficult. A representative from the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum stated that what drivers might see in the future is likely limited to short hops rather than sustained flight.
paragraphs.zh: 其他致力於電動垂直起降飛行器（簡稱 eVTOL）的公司指出，從垂直升空到向前移動的轉變極為困難。來自史密森尼國家航空太空博物館（Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum）的代表表示，駕駛員未來可能看到的很可能僅限於短距離跳躍，而非持續飛行。

paragraphs.en: Musk stated that the new vehicle will go into production in 2028, although the company has often missed its previous release timelines. Whether the automobile can successfully combine high-speed ground travel with real flying capability remains to be proven.
paragraphs.zh: 馬斯克表示該新車將於 2028 年投入生產，儘管該公司過去經常錯過先前的發布時間表。這輛汽車能否成功結合高速地面行駛與真正的飛行能力，仍有待證明。

grammar.explain: 此句使用「be 動詞 + 過去分詞 (is designed)」構成被動語態，表達車輛是被設計成具備特定功能。
grammar.example: The vehicle is designed to go from 0 to 60 mph in less than a second and features unique capabilities that allow it to jump and hover using specialized air jets.

grammar.explain: 此句使用逗號隔開的 V-ing 分詞構句 (known as eVTOLs)，用來補充說明前面的名詞。
grammar.example: Other companies working on electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, known as eVTOLs, point out that the transition from vertical lifting to forward movement is extremely difficult.
